text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing steady GPU memory growth on H100 during long-chat perf runs with paged KV enabled. Memory climbs ~200MB every ~3 minutes on 16k seq lengths and doesn't stabilize. Repro attached (local run).

nina: Can you drop the minimal repro (model, batch, env flags)? also which runtime build?

alex: Model: mix-lm-30B (paged-attn enabled), batch=1, prompt ~32 tokens then generate to 16k. Runtime: master@2026-03-10 (commit 9f3b7). Env: KV_PAGING=1, KV_REUSE_WINDOW=60000, ASYNC_EVICT=1. Repro cmd: `./tools/longctx_harness --model mix-lm-30B --seq 16384 --batch 1 --rt-args="--kv-paging"`

hao: OK. Do you have nvprof/nsys traces? also does A100 behave the same? MI250X?

alex: Quick paste from nvprof timeline (abbrev):
```
[00:00:12] alloc_kv_page gid=0x7f9 evict_candidate page=0x2ab
[00:00:13] async_evict_submit id=42 -> submit
[00:00:13] evict_complete id=42 -> mark_free
[00:00:13] pt_remap owner_update page=0x2ab -> owner=0x11
[00:00:13] pt_remap owner_update page=0x2ab -> owner=0x11  <-- duplicate
[00:00:14] alloc_kv_page gid=0x7f9 page=0x2ab reused
[00:00:15] use_kv_page gid=0x7f9 kv_slot=0x50
[00:03:12] memory +200MB
```
There's repeated pt_remap/owner_update logs and later the same physical page gets reused while some stale mapping remains.

lisa: That log looks like the evict completion is racing with PT updates — duplicates imply the callback replayed or wasn't idempotent. On H100 we also see different segstride alignment which can change eviction grouping; eviction order divergence could leave ghost refs. Hypothesis: async evict completion doesn't properly fence page table writes on H100 path.

nina: If it's a race, an easy A/B is `ASYNC_EVICT=0` (force sync evict); can you run A100/H100 with that and compare mem drift and p99 latency?

alex: Ran A100 with ASYNC_EVICT=0: memory drift drops to ~30MB per 3m (vs 200MB), but p99 latency increased ~12ms (steady). H100 with same flag also improves stability but p99 hit larger. Numbers:
- A100 async=1: +200MB/3m, p99=48ms
- A100 async=0: +30MB/3m, p99=60ms
- H100 async=1: +220MB/3m, p99=42ms
- H100 async=0: +35MB/3m, p99=70ms
so sync evict mitigates leak but with notable latency cost.

hao: Interesting. MI250X? I recall MI250 had stronger page remap ordering but different kernel tiling; may not show same dup logs. If H100 relies on NV driver async semantics that let callbacks reorder, we could be hitting an ordering bug. Also check `pt->owner` update path: are we doing a compare-exchange or blind store?

lisa: Code note: there's a `pt_update()` that does `pt[p] = owner;` followed by an `atomic_dec(free_count)` in evict_complete. If evict_complete runs concurrently twice for the same page (duplicate submit), the second will see owner already set and early-return — but if duplicate submit happens before pt_update commits to device-visible mapping, you could get reuse before mapping cleared. Suggest adding explicit device-host sync point / memory fence in evict_complete and making pt_update idempotent.

nina: Could also be fragmentation + reuse window shrink: long context plus many small prefix caches create lots of tiny pages; our LRU scan may skip small holes and fragmentation grows. Might explain why async evict exposes it (we reassign pages quickly). Suggest bumping KV_REUSE_WINDOW to 120000 for an experiment and enable a compact-on-threshold path.

alex: Tried bumping KV_REUSE_WINDOW to 120000 on A100: reduced churn but mem still grows slowly. Combining `KV_REUSE_WINDOW=120000` + `ASYNC_EVICT=0` basically stabilizes memory but p99 penalty compounds.

hao: Another angle: kernel selection and batching heuristics might change KV allocation patterns. With long seqs we switch to tiled-kernel X which does more partial-cache writes; perhaps these generate more metadata ops and race windows. Can you capture `--nvtx` traces focused on kernel names and `kvcache_*` events? Also run with `KV_PAGE_DEBUG=1` to capture pt ops.

alex: Attached NVTX slice shows frequent `kvcache_async_evict` and `kvpage_reuse` bursts aligned with the tiled attention kernels. Patch idea: coalesce async_evict submissions and add per-page in-flight flag so duplicates aren't submitted. Simple lockless CAS on page->inflight might avoid duplicate callbacks.

lisa: Good. If duplicate submissions are root cause, that would explain the repeated owner_update logs. However we should still add a defensive fence in pt_update; hardware ordering differs H100 vs A100 vs MI250X. I'll prototype `page->inflight` CAS + a `device_fence()` in evict_complete.

nina: For immediate mitigation in prod for high-longctx customers: enable `KV_PAGE_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.8` to force compaction sooner and set `ASYNC_EVICT=0` in H100 pools until we patch. Add an observability dashboard for `pg_frag_ratio` and `inflight_evicts` so we can see the effect.

alex: Filed an issue and attached repro trace: https://redwood-internal/issue/ENGRT-4321 (repro + nvprof). Assigning to eng-runtime/kv-pager. Can kv-ci-bot kick off cross-arch runs (H100, A100, MI250X) with the three configs: baseline, sync-evict, inflight-cas-prototype?

kv-ci-bot: Scheduled CI matrix job ENGRT-4321: runs queued on h100/24g, a100/40g, mi250x/128g; will post results to the ticket when complete. ETA ~3 hours. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks — I'll follow up with traces and proposed PR with CAS+fence. :thumbsup:
